## Summary

Pegatron is a Taiwanese contract manufacturer headquartered in Beitou District, Taipei, created in ASUS's 2008 restructuring and spun off from ASUS on 1 June 2010; it makes laptops, desktops, netbooks and game consoles, as well as smartphones, set-top boxes and cable modems [1]. Apple is a customer, with Pegatron's India plant taking on some iPhone production, and Pegatron supplies components to Tesla [1]. The IEEE registry lists 25 MA-L blocks to "PEGATRON CORPORATION" at 76 Ligong Street, Beitou, Taipei [2].

Because Pegatron builds for other brands, a MAC in its blocks may sit in a product sold under another name: WikiDevi lists under Pegatron devices sold by ASUS, Arris, Cisco, Netgear, Technicolor, ZyXEL and Sagemcom, and gives Pegatron the FCC grantee code VUI [3]. Its Wi-Fi modules include the UPWL6024 (Broadcom BCM43224, 802.11a/b/g/n) in the Virgin Media Super Hub 1, the UPWL6025 (Broadcom BCM43225) in the Netgear CG3000D, and the UPWL6580 (Atheros AR9580, FCC ID VUIUPWL6580) in the Cisco DPC3939 and Virgin Media Super Hub 2 [4][5][6].

No Pegatron-specific security advisory was found by the sources consulted, and randomization behaviour is not documented; the FCC ID databases refused automated access from this session.
